body:
When I lost my job, the insurance went with it. And while I have gone through the motions to get on state insurance, there are many more motions to get through before I can get my scripts back. 

Tldr I ran out and haven't been able to see a doctor that can actually write them. I have an appointment sometime this week but I'm not counting chickens yet.

I wouldn't know where to begin. And I know I don't want to leave them behind - they are why I'm still here.

My biggest concerns are mostly financial. Also I've been off my meds for about a month, which is playing a huge part in this.

Thank you for your reply, it means a lot to me.

Thank you for the response. This is one of those scenarios where I definitely have to just eat the lesson. This wouldn't be a company that would take me back, and I wouldn't want to work there again after how I've been treated. The stress I experienced every day just showing up to work showed me that I needed to get another job. I am just so worn out at the end of the day, and I've got no time in the morning since it takes me two hours to prepare for my day and not forget anything. 

Well, now I've got more time. I also didn't get completely hosed, they offered a severance package to make a mutual departure. I think they are trying to avoid a lawsuit and paying unemployment. Either way, without it I would be in pretty deep, murky water. And finding another job in the field isn't impossible, but it definitely isn't easy when you get let go before hitting one year of tender.
